h1: The 6 Best Printers for Dorm Rooms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Dorm Room Printers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six compact printers for dorm rooms compared on footprint, wireless setup, scanning, duplex printing and ink or cartridge costs.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the best pick for most students: wireless, duplex and compact. The TS6520 adds a small display for shared rooms, the TR4720 suits anyone scanning multi-page documents, and the inkless MT610Pro is a backup for light printing.
intro: Dorm printers fail on the boring details. A printer that needs a USB cable to your laptop, or a wide body that will not fit on a standard desk shelf, ends up in the closet by October. Wireless setup and a small footprint matter more here than print speed.

We reviewed eight printers and kept six that suit a dorm. We ranked them on the spec sheets and owner-reported use, focusing on size, wireless and phone printing, scanning, two-sided printing and how much ongoing ink or cartridge hassle each one brings.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Prints, copies, scans and duplexes in a body that fits a dorm desk.
products.description:
The TS4320 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one that prints, copies and scans, with two-sided printing built in. It has a compact desktop footprint and a one-year limited warranty.

It wins over the TS6520 because it covers the same everyday jobs at the same price range without paying for extra features a student seldom uses. It gives up the display of the pricier TS6520, so setup relies on the phone app.

Choose it if you want one dependable machine for essays, forms and the occasional scan. Look elsewhere if you share the printer with several roommates.
products.idealFor: Most dorm students who want one all-round printer.
products.skipIf: A shared printer needs a screen for menus.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen makes a shared printer far less confusing.
products.description:
The TS6520 adds a 1.42 inch OLED display to a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with duplex printing and copy and scan functions. The design stays compact.

It ranks just under the TS4320 only because most solo students never use the screen, and it sits in the same price range. For roommates the display lets anyone check status or change settings without the app.

Pick it when two or more people share the machine. If you are the only user, the TS4320 does the same work without the extra cost of the screen.
products.idealFor: Shared dorm rooms with several users.
products.skipIf: You live alone and rarely touch settings.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: An automatic document feeder turns multi-page scanning into a one-step job.
products.description:
The TR4720 pairs wireless printing with an auto document feeder, built-in fax and mobile printing. It prints, scans, copies and faxes, and comes in a white finish.

It ranks third because the feeder makes it bulkier than the TS-series models, which matters on a small desk. In return you can load a stack of signed pages and scan them without lifting the lid for each sheet.

Best for students who scan lease paperwork, forms or lab notes often. If you mostly print, the TS4320 saves space.
products.idealFor: Students who scan multi-page documents regularly.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A full wireless all-in-one that keeps the starting cost low.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 prints, scans and copies wirelessly and includes a three-month Instant Ink trial. It is a compact home design with AI-capable features listed.

It ranks fourth because the listing does not mention duplex printing, which the Canon models above offer. The Instant Ink trial can lower early ink costs, but it is a subscription you need to manage after the trial.

A good fit for budget-minded students who want a full machine without extra frills. Skip it if two-sided printing is a priority.
products.idealFor: Budget students who want a full all-in-one.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: The lightest, simplest Canon, easy to pack at semester's end.
products.description:
The TS3720 is a basic wireless color inkjet all-in-one with a compact, lightweight body in white. It prints, scans and copies and focuses on plain home printing.

It sits below the TS4320 because it drops the duplex support and extras listed on that model. The upside is bulk, since it is the easiest of the Canons to carry up a dorm staircase.

Good for students who change rooms each year and print only occasionally. If your course load is print-heavy, the TS4320 saves paper and time.
products.skipIf: You print large volumes of coursework.

products.name: Inkless Portable Printer for Travel (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: No ink, no toner, just a thermal backup for occasional pages.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is a Bluetooth thermal printer that needs no ink or toner cartridges. It prints Letter and A4 at 300 DPI and works with iOS, Android and laptops.

It ranks last because it is not a copier or scanner, and thermal output is meant for plain documents rather than color work. Its advantage is size and zero cartridge shopping.

Best as a lightweight backup for students who rely mostly on campus print stations. If you need scanning or color, one of the Canon all-in-ones is the better choice.
products.idealFor: Students who mostly use campus printing.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or color output.

whatMatters.detail: A dorm desk shelf is often narrower than a standard printer, and a heavy machine is hard to move at semester's end. Measure the space and compare it with the listing dimensions. Compact and lightweight wording in the specs is a helpful signal.

Wireless printing lets you send documents from a laptop or phone without a cable. In a shared room this avoids swapping cords between roommates. Check the listing for Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and for mobile printing support.

Duplex means the printer prints on both sides of the paper automatically. It halves your paper use on long readings and makes thick packets easier to handle. Look for the word duplex or 2-sided in the specs, since it is missing on some cheaper models.

A flatbed scanner handles single sheets, while an auto document feeder takes a stack. For lease forms or signed pages a feeder saves minutes each time. Check whether the listing mentions a feeder or only a flatbed.

Inkjets are cheap to buy, but replacement cartridges add up, and subscriptions bill monthly. Inkless thermal printers avoid cartridges but only print simple documents. Decide how much you really print before choosing.

howToChoose.intro: How often you print decides how much machine you need.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Inkjets print in color, scan and copy, but need cartridges. The Canon TS4320, TS6520, TR4720, TS3720 and the HP DeskJet 4355 are all inkjet all-in-ones.

cards.label: Inkless thermal
cards.text: Thermal printers use heat on special paper, so there are no cartridges, but they cannot scan or print color. The MT610Pro is the only one here.

howToChoose.note: Most students should choose an inkjet unless printing is rare.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Mobile and tablet printing support plus wireless setup so you can print without a laptop.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon TR4720 lists mobile printing support outright, and the MT610Pro works with iOS and Android over Bluetooth.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Several people share the printer, which favors the Canon TS6520 display, or you scan stacks, which favors the TR4720 feeder.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print rarely. The HP DeskJet 4355 or Canon TS3720 cover basics, and the MT610Pro skips cartridges completely.

faq.q: Do dorm printers need a cable?
faq.a: Not the wireless ones. The Canon models and the HP DeskJet 4355 join your Wi-Fi, while the MT610Pro uses Bluetooth. Check that your dorm network allows device connections before buying.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying on price without checking size. A printer that does not fit your desk shelf becomes floor clutter, so measure first.

faq.q: Is the TS6520 worth it over the TS4320?
faq.a: Only for shared rooms. The display helps roommates manage settings, but a solo student gets the same prints from the cheaper TS4320.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless printer in a dorm?
faq.a: Use the manufacturer's phone app to join the printer to your Wi-Fi, then add it on your laptop. Some campus networks need a device registration step first.

faq.q: How do I keep ink costs down?
faq.a: Print in draft mode for notes, use duplex printing and avoid full-color pages. The HP Instant Ink trial can help early on, but track the plan after it ends.

faq.q: Can an inkless printer replace a normal one?
faq.a: For plain text documents, yes. It cannot scan, copy or print color, so most students will still want an inkjet for forms and projects.

finalTake: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the best dorm printer for most students: wireless, duplex and small. Choose the TS6520 for shared rooms and the TR4720 for heavy scanning. Keep the MT610Pro in mind only as a light backup if campus printing already covers your needs.
